walkthroughs.body_html: Kosher rules come from the Torah. Allowed animals include cows, sheep and chickens; forbidden ones include pork and shellfish. Meat and dairy must not be eaten together. Food prepared the right way is kosher; food that breaks the rules is treif.

At 13, a Jewish boy becomes a 'son of the commandment' — Bar Mitzvah. He reads from the Torah in the synagogue for the first time. Girls often celebrate Bat Mitzvah at 12. Both mark moving into religious adulthood.
Two famous Jewish symbols are the Star of David (six-pointed star) and the Menorah (seven-branched lampstand from the ancient Temple). A nine-branched menorah called a hanukiah is used at Hanukkah.

Substance dualism means men and women are different.
